about.what: Every endpoint REEP's FastAPI app serves, classified by role, feature, CRUD operation, gate, tables, external systems and calling screen -- the source of docs/diagrams/n8n/reep-roles-features-crud.n8n.json.
about.method: Route table read from the running app (app.routes, 379 method+path rows incl. 3 WebSockets and the /api/v1/auth aliases); each handler classified from its source by one agent and then re-checked by a second, adversarial agent reading the same guards (25 corrections applied). Lines are the handler's def line at that commit.

vocabulary.roles: STUDENT, FACULTY (users.role MENTOR), ALUMNI, MAIN_ADMIN (users.role ADMIN), PUBLIC (no session), ANY_SIGNED_IN, SYSTEM
vocabulary.faculty_access: NONE | ALWAYS | MENTOR_GROUP (rule 2: own mentees) | GRANT (only by a Governance grant of the capability) | OWN_ONLY (the faculty member's own rows)
vocabulary.crud: CREATE | READ | UPDATE (incl. approve, decide, submit, restore) | DELETE (incl. revoke, remove, purge) | ACTION (sign-in, codes, sockets, asking the agent)

endpoints.summary: Edits a course's code, name, duration or status (archive/restore), refusing a duplicate code in the department.
Lists the specializations under one course, each with its batch count.
Creates a specialization under a course, refusing a duplicate code within that course.
Edits a specialization's code, name or status (archive/restore); no Angular screen calls it today.
Lists the configurable alert thresholds, optionally for one batch, read by the Analytics screen's alert-rules dialog.
Creates or updates the threshold, severity and on/off switch of one alert rule for one batch.
Returns the Analytics header tiles (students, pending applications, faculty, badges, evidence awaiting, placed %) narrowed to the caller's reach.
Returns the KPI strip (placement rate, median/highest CTC, readiness %, attendance, pending approvals) with deltas against the previous window, scoped to the reach.
Returns weekly attendance %, skilling hours, approved offers and this week's placement-ready % for the students in reach.
Lists the approved certification catalogue within the caller's reach (programme-wide rows always visible), with claim counts, optionally filtered to one course.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.catalogue) + _resolve_certification_scope (scoped holder must name a college/course in reach)
endpoints.summary: Adds an external certification that counts towards a badge, programme-wide or for one college/course, audited.
Edits a certification in the catalogue (name, provider, badge, stage, active, college/course scope), fenced on both old and new reach, audited.
Returns a filtered, paginated page of the append-only audit trail (actor, action, target, date range), newest first, without writing an event of its own.
Downloads the same filtered audit query as a formula-injection-hardened CSV (refused over 10,000 rows) and records the download itself as an audit event.
Returns one audit event with its before/after snapshots and metadata.
Returns the 48-badge catalogue from code (no database read) so the Catalogue screen's certification form can map a certification to a badge.
Returns programme-wide badge counts by category and average capability scores per checkpoint; no screen calls it today.
Downloads one row per student with points, badges per category and mean growth from baseline, and records an export receipt.
Lists every taught course with its enrolment count and the certifications mapped to it.
Returns all 48 code-defined badges with whether each is enabled for the given course.
Upserts whether one badge applies to one course (writes an enabled=true row rather than deleting), audited.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.catalogue) + _course_within_reach on both from_course and to_course
endpoints.summary: Copies certifications, badge switches and/or stage rules from one programme to another, additive only (existing rows skipped), with a ?dry_run preview.
Flat list of every programme in the caller's reach with counts of its certifications, badge overrides and stage rules (also the Jobs sheet's course picker).
Lists the semester-to-REEP-stage rules for every course in reach, optionally one course.
Upserts the REEP stage for one semester of one course, used when a batch is promoted, audited.
Removes a 'semester N of this course is stage S' rule, audited.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.catalogue) + scope_filter must be programme-wide (a scoped grant is refused)
endpoints.summary: Imports a CSV of taught subjects into the global courses table (create or update by code), dry run by default, reporting every row.
Lists every batch with its display label and student count, used as the batch picker on several admin screens (not scope-narrowed).
Lists batches missing a hierarchy level that HIERARCHY_LEVELS currently marks required (empty while nothing is required).
Lists batches that belong to no department yet so the office can file them.

Deletes a batch only when no student (including a removed one) is seated in it, refusing with 409 otherwise, and writes an audit row; note it does not apply the B1.4 reach target, so any admin.students holder may delete any empty batch.
Edits a batch's name, year label, dates or department/course/specialization links, deriving ancestors and refusing an edit that widens the required-level gap.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.students) + _cohort_or_404 + assert_batch_within_reach (all-or-nothing scope over the batch)
endpoints.summary: Graduates every student on a batch (dry_run=true previews): students.status GRADUATED, users.role ALUMNI, token_version bumped to sign them out, a history row each and cohorts.status GRADUATED; no alumni profile is created.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.students) + _cohort_or_404 + assert_batch_within_reach (all-or-nothing scope over the batch)
endpoints.summary: Moves every student in a batch up one semester (except those held back), applying stage rules, refusing anyone already at the course's last semester, with a dry-run preflight panel; writes one history row per student and an audit event.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.students) + _cohort_or_404 + assert_batch_within_reach (all-or-nothing scope over the batch)
endpoints.summary: Lists every promote / graduate / ungraduate move recorded against the students seated in one batch, newest first, with who did it and why.
Lists the students seated in one batch (name, email, USN, stage) for the seating panel.

Applies one action (move to another batch, assign or release faculty, set stage, or set semester) to every non-removed student in a batch, refused whole if any student is outside the caller's reach, writing per-student mentor history and one audit row.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.students) + _cohort_or_404 + assert_batch_within_reach (all-or-nothing scope over the batch)
endpoints.summary: Takes a batch's graduation back within 30 days of it being pressed (all or nothing): students back to ACTIVE and role STUDENT, sessions retired, batch ACTIVE; any alumni profile the graduates filled in is kept and counted.
Lists every college, archived ones included, with its department count and email domains.
Creates a college with its code, name, campus, contact and email domains, refusing a duplicate code.
Edits a college's code, name, campus, contact, email domains or status (archive/restore).
Lists the staff holding any college-admin capability scoped to this college, with each grant's approval state and the keys still missing.
Grants a staff account the fixed set of college-scoped admin.* capabilities with one reason and one audit row per grant (live at once from the Main Admin, PII keys pending when a deputy appoints).

Permanently deletes a college and its structure after spending the Main Admin's emailed six-digit code, refusing (409) while any student, faculty account or open application is still under it, and writes an audit row.

Counts what deleting a college would remove (its departments, courses, specializations, batches and their configuration), what would only lose its pointer, and the blockers (seated students, filed faculty, open applications) that refuse it; destroys nothing.
Lists the departments of one college, each with its batch count.
Creates a department under a college, refusing a duplicate code within that college.
Returns the placement gates set for a course, college or the programme (walking that chain), or 404 when nothing has been set.
Writes a new set of placement gates for a course, college or the programme (programme-wide is Main Admin only), deactivating the previous set and auditing the change.
Lists every set of placement gates ever written (superseded ones marked inactive), newest first, optionally for one course or college.
Mails the signed-in Main Admin's own address a six-digit code that authorises exactly one permanent deletion (second factor), superseding any earlier code.
Lists every department in every college with a disambiguated label, for one-control department pickers.
Edits a department's code, name, head or status (archive/restore); no Angular screen calls it today.
Lists the courses (degree programmes) under one department, each with its specialization count.
Creates a course (degree programme) under a department, refusing a duplicate code within that department.
Lists the batches under one department with their composed label, student count and any missing required levels.
Creates a batch under a department with its year label, dates, degree level and optional course/specialization, deriving the ancestry.
Lists the export receipts (who downloaded which extract, rows, PII or not); a programme-wide holder sees all, a narrowed holder only their own.
Downloads per-student Time Allocation Ledger compliance as CSV within the caller's reach, dropping name/USN unless PII is allowed, and writes an export receipt.
Downloads every submitted offer as CSV (optionally one batch) within the caller's reach and records an export receipt.
Downloads the admitted-students and mentor map as CSV within the caller's reach and records an export receipt.
Lists every faculty (MENTOR) account with where it is filed and its disabled state, unfiled first; ?unfiled=true and ?removed=true narrow the list.
Creates a MENTOR login filed under a required department, fenced to the college's email domains, and returns its activation link (emailed when mail is configured).
Edits a faculty member's name, address, designation or department filing; an address change is domain-fenced and signs the account out everywhere.
Serves the capability and student-feature catalogues (from code constants, no table) plus the minimum reason length for the console's pickers.
Resolves what one staff account actually holds (role baseline + derived mentor functions + live grants); no Angular screen calls it.
Lists every student feature override with its target label, who set it and how many students it affects.
Upserts a student feature override (on/off at one rung of the spine, with reason and optional student message); refused 422 for a feature no router enforces.
Hard-deletes one student feature override so the next rung up decides again, writing an audit row first; the Main Admin by baseline or a faculty deputy granted admin.governance.
Lists every unrevoked, unexpired capability grant, pending second-approval ones included, with subject, reach and granter.

Grants one capability to staff users and/or access groups with a 20+ character reason and optional scope/expiry; the Main Admin's grants are live at once, a deputy's carries_pii grant is written pending_approval.
Activates a pending (deputy-made, carries_pii) grant as the second signature; a deputy cannot approve their own grant, the Main Admin can.
Moves a live grant's expiry and/or review date with a freshly typed reason; a lapsed grant must be granted again (409).
Revokes a capability grant by stamping revoked_at/by/reason (the row is kept) and audits it.
Lists access groups with their staff members and the active capabilities each group holds.
Creates a named access group (unique name) that capabilities can later be granted to.
Adds staff accounts to an access group with a required reason, handing them every capability the group holds; each addition is audited.
Removes a staff account from an access group (taking away every capability the group holds) and audits it.
Returns every college/department/course/specialization/batch rung with a live student count, used as the scope picker for grants and feature switches.
Returns the two action queues: grants pending a second approval and active grants expiring or due for review within the horizon (also counted on the admin Home tile).
Lists every MENTOR and ADMIN account as the people a capability can be granted to.
Returns the HIERARCHY_LEVELS constant (which of Course and Specialization a new batch must name) so the batch form builds its validators from it.
Lists the attendance and marks import runs within the caller's reach, newest first, with their counts and who ran them.

Uploads an attendance or marks spreadsheet for one batch, parses and judges every line against the roster and subject catalogue, and saves the run and its judged rows without touching any student record.
Builds and downloads a blank Excel template (header, example line, column notes) for an attendance or marks import.
Writes a previewed run's accepted lines into students' attendance or semester marks (upsert) in one audited transaction and marks the run applied; a second apply is refused.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.imports) + require_capability(admin.imports, target=ancestry_of_cohort) (student names only with admin.students)
endpoints.summary: Downloads a CSV of every refused or warned line of an import run (name column withheld without admin.students) and records an export receipt.

Returns a college's default interview policy and its per-course overrides (transcript/audio storage, retention, daily and attempt caps, time limit) plus the effective default and whether the server can record at all.

Creates or updates a college's default interview policy (storage scopes, retention, caps, time limit), refusing an attempt cap below the daily cap, with an audit row; changes apply to interviews opened after the save.
Creates or updates one course's interview policy row that shadows the college default, inheriting omitted fields from what currently governs that course, with an audit row.
Lists every question on one interview track, enabled or not, in interview order, narrowed to the caller's college reach.
Adds one question (track, phase, text) to the end of a track's bank, stamped with the track and college, audited.
Parses pasted lines (or a file's text) into many questions appended to a track, reporting unreadable lines by number without storing them, each added row audited.
Rewrites the position of every question on a track from a complete ordered id list (the order the interviewer covers them); unlike the other bank writes it writes no audit row.
Lists every interviewer track the caller may see (rows plus the shipped matrix constants) with question counts and an editable flag.
Creates a new interviewer track (code, persona, Nova voice, syllabus) hung on a college/course/specialization rung, audited.
Deletes an interviewer track that no interview has ever used (409 otherwise, disable instead); its bank questions survive with track_id nulled.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.interview_questions) + _require_reach on the row as it stands and as it would be
endpoints.summary: Edits a track's label, persona, frameworks, voice, syllabus, enabled flag, position or spine mapping (code is immutable), audited.
Removes a question from the bank after auditing its before-image.
Edits a question's text, phase or enabled flag, refused for a question outside the caller's reach, audited with before/after.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.interviews) + scope_filter(admin.interviews); _records_query also narrows a MENTOR to their own mentor group
endpoints.summary: Paginated, filterable grid of every mock interview the caller may see (scope header set); a granted faculty member is still narrowed to their own mentees.
Downloads a CSV of interview score summaries (no transcript or reasoning), names only if the caller may see personal columns, and writes an export receipt.
Returns the KPI tiles (counts by status, students, recorded, scored, averages by track) over exactly the rows the grid would show.
Lists every job posting the caller's reach covers, newest first, with its applicant count and college/course labels.
Publishes a new job posting (optionally limited to a college, course or tracks) that appears at once on the student and alumni job boards.
Deletes a job posting, refused with 409 once any student has applied (close it instead); no scope reach check, unlike close.
Marks a posting closed so it leaves the student and alumni boards while keeping applications, idempotently and with an audit event.
Lists recorded leave allowances (entitled, consumed, remaining) for staff and students, filterable by year, person, department and kind, paged.
Upserts one person's leave allowance for a kind and academic year (entitled and optionally consumed days) and audits the change.
Creates one leave allowance of a kind and year for every staff member and/or student in a department, skipping anyone who already has one (never overwrites consumed days).
Deletes one recorded leave allowance (which stops the submit path checking that person's requests of that kind, unlike setting it to zero) and audits the before-image.
Lists a college's recorded closed and explicitly open days within an optional date range.
Records or corrects one day on a college's academic calendar (holiday or working day, with a label), which the leave submit path counts working days against.
Removes one holiday/working-day entry from a college's academic calendar and audits it.
Returns the console's leave-policy summary for an academic year: printed leave kinds, how many allowances and people are recorded, and holiday/working-day counts per college.
Lists the last N messages REEP tried to send, newest first, filterable by kind, recipient prefix and failed-only.
The Main Admin removes an address from Amazon SES's account suppression list so mail can reach it again, and the act is written to the audit trail (409 when no mail transport is configured).
Asks SES live whether one address is on the account suppression list, answering checked:false when the question could not be put.
Lists every faculty account within reach with capacity, placement and each assigned mentee's attendance, verified skills and logged hours (gated on admin.analytics, not admin.mentors).
Returns the placement funnel, CTC figures, by-track split, recent offers and top recruiters for the students in reach, optionally by batch and year.

Lists the student roster (name, email, USN, batch, department, faculty, stage, semester), narrowed to the caller's grant reach with an X-Reep-Scope header, filterable by batch, unseated, search text or ?removed=true for the Restore list.

Files up to 500 explicitly named students (seated or not) under one department, refusing the whole call if any id is missing or a seated student's batch contradicts it; no screen calls it and it applies no per-student reach target.
Lists students who sit in no batch, the pool the seating panel picks from.

Edits one student's name, college email, USN, batch, department, second specialization, assigned faculty, stage and semester, with the domain fence, uniqueness, semester ceiling and same-college mentor checks, recording mentor history and an audit row.

Returns one student's complete record (identity, login, profile, documents, semesters, readiness, open items, mentor and history, recent audit) in one read; a faculty member needs a Governance grant of admin.student_records AND still sees only their own mentees under rule 2.
Seats a student in a batch, or releases them with a null cohort_id.

Spends the emailed code, then destroys the student's stored files and interview/platform recordings and deletes every row the deletion walk reaches, stamps the document manifest released and writes an audit before-image.

Runs the same per-account deletion walk the permanent delete runs, by student id, and returns the counts and plain-language consequences the delete dialog prints before the button; refuses the Main Admin and the caller's own account.

Records a reason-required cap reset that moves the start of one student's rolling 24-hour interview window forward, giving their practice attempts back; a granted faculty member must also mentor that student (rule 2).

Assigns a student to a same-college faculty member (creating the mentor group on first use) or releases them, with a required reason, recording the history spell, a 90-day handover read grant for the previous mentor, and an audit event.
Returns every mentor spell a student has had, newest first, with who opened and closed each and why.

Soft-removes a student with a written reason: stamps users.deleted_at, bumps token_version and revokes live links so they cannot sign in, hides them from every roster and leaderboard, and keeps every record for Restore.
Clears a removed student's deleted_at so they return to every screen with nothing lost (still barred if separately disabled), and audits it.
Renders a student's latest REEP resume to PDF locally; a faculty holder of the granted Analytics screen can only fetch their own mentees'.
Returns one student's last six weeks of attendance and ledger hours plus verified skills by category; a granted faculty member sees only their own mentees.
Lists every student the caller's grant reaches with their Strengths/Weaknesses/Opportunities/Challenges lines, filterable by batch, semester and search, optionally paged via headers.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.swoc) + require_capability(admin.swoc, target=ancestry_of_student) + _assert_owns (author or Main Admin)
endpoints.summary: Deletes one SWOC line about a student within the caller's reach, allowed only to its author or the Main Admin (an authorless line is the Main Admin's alone), with a before-image audit row.

endpoints.guard: require_capability(admin.swoc) + require_capability(admin.swoc, target=ancestry_of_student) + _assert_owns (author or Main Admin)
endpoints.summary: Edits a SWOC line's text, weight or links to a skill, interview or job, allowed to its author or the Main Admin, writing a revision row and an audit row.
Adds a SWOC line about a student, stamping the viewpoint as MENTOR only when the author mentors that student (otherwise PLACEMENT) and the student's current semester, with an audit row.
Returns every recorded edit (before/after) to the lines on one student's SWOC board, newest first, scoped like the board itself.
Lists students within reach who have no faculty mentor yet, optionally filtered and paged, as the pool the assignment picker draws from.

Mints (superseding any older one) a staff account's first-password activation link, emails it when mail is configured and returns it to show on screen; refuses students, disabled accounts and accounts that already hold a password.

Spends the emailed code and permanently deletes a non-admin account (faculty on screen) with its files and rows; a faculty member's mentees are released and the notes they wrote about students go with them.

Runs the per-account deletion walk by user id (used for faculty, works for any non-admin account) and returns what a permanent delete would take, including mentees released and meeting notes deleted with a faculty member.

Offboards an account with a required reason: stamps disabled_at, signs out every device, spends outstanding links and releases a faculty member's mentees to the unassigned pool; refuses the Main Admin and oneself.
Switches a disabled account back on within 90 days of disabling, without restoring any capability grants.
Writes a user's free-text designation and department lines that the leave form prints; no Angular screen calls it today.
Soft-removes an account with a written reason (off every list, cannot sign in, rows kept); a removed faculty member's mentees are released to the unassigned pool.
Brings a removed account back onto every list with all its records (mentees released at removal are not re-assigned), and audits it.
Bumps an account's token_version so every session it holds is retired, without touching its password.

endpoints.guard: _require_agent_access: require_capability(mentor.agent) for MENTOR/ADMIN; require_feature(student.agent) for STUDENT; llm_rate_limited
endpoints.summary: Runs the structured, tool-backed assistant on a question (student-record intents only for students, grounded KB answers for everyone), persists both turns and one agent run, and returns answer, actions, sources and a run_id.

endpoints.guard: _require_agent_access: require_capability(mentor.agent) for MENTOR/ADMIN; require_feature(student.agent) for STUDENT; llm_rate_limited
endpoints.summary: Free-form LLM chat on the caller's server-owned conversation, persisting the turns and an agent run; retained for rollback, no screen calls it.

endpoints.guard: _require_agent_access: require_capability(mentor.agent) for MENTOR/ADMIN; require_feature(student.agent) for STUDENT; llm_rate_limited
endpoints.summary: Server-Sent Events variant of the free-form chat that streams the reply token by token; dead endpoint with no caller.
Soft-clears the caller's own assistant conversation (the thread both the typed agent and the mock interviewer write into) so the next chat starts fresh.

endpoints.guard: get_current_session + caller must own the agent run (404 otherwise)
endpoints.summary: Records (upserts) a helpful / not helpful / report rating with a PII-redacted note against one of the caller's own agent runs.
Returns the caller's own current conversation turns, typed agent and mock-interview turns alike.
Lets a student search the approved Knowledge Base (hybrid full-text plus pgvector) for policy and FAQ chunks; test-only, no screen calls it.
Gives the Main Admin aggregate assistant health: run counts, resolution and refusal rates, latency, breakdowns by intent/model/status, turns per channel and feedback tallies.
Lists the caller's own 50 most recent assistant runs as an audit trail; no screen calls it.
Lists the open job postings an alumnus may see, scoped to their old college/course/track through the linked student row (whole open board if unlinked), without match % or eligibility.
Returns the alumnus's own profile, with created:false until one is saved, which is what sends the client to the first-login create-profile form.

Creates the alumnus's profile on first sign-in (company plus a required resume) and updates it afterwards, replacing the single resume in place and recording the old file as released in the document manifest.
Streams the alumnus's own resume file from the document store as an attachment download.

endpoints.guard: activation token (auth_tokens, PURPOSE_ACTIVATION); refuses STUDENT, an account already holding a password, and a barred account
endpoints.summary: Consumes a staff activation link to set the account's first password and signs it in (retiring any other device), refusing students, accounts that already have a password and disabled or removed accounts.

endpoints.guard: get_current_session + exactly one proof (emailed code or current password)
endpoints.summary: Changes the signed-in account's own password given either the emailed change code or the current password (never both), signs out every other device and re-issues this device's session.
Mails a six-digit code authorising a password change to the address on the signed-in account (never one from the request), refusing 409 for an account that holds no password yet.

Always answers the same 202 sentence, and in the background mails a reset link to an active password account or, for a password-less student, the onboarding setup link; staff without a password and barred accounts get nothing.

verb_by_lane.ACCOUNT: email me a setup link (no password yet)

endpoints.guard: none (public; single-use state cookie + nonce, verified Google ID token, roster lookup, google_sub pin)
endpoints.summary: Google redirects here after consent; the server verifies the ID token, admits only an email already on the roster (pinning google_sub on first use), retires other sessions, records the sign-in, optionally mails a sign-in alert, sets the reep_session cookie and redirects to the role's home. Legacy alias of /api/auth/sso/google/callback, hidden from the schema; Google itself only calls the canonical path.

endpoints.guard: none (public; refuses with /login?error=sso_config when Google is not configured)
endpoints.summary: Mints a state and nonce, stores them in a short-lived cookie and redirects the browser to Google's consent screen. Legacy alias of /api/auth/sso/google, hidden from the OpenAPI schema.

Tells the login screen whether Google sign-in is configured, whether the password door is open (derived from whether any account holds a real scrypt hash) and the institution's mail domain. Legacy alias of /api/auth/sso/status, hidden from the schema.

endpoints.guard: get_current_session (refused 409 unless the account holds a real password and the password door is open)
endpoints.summary: Clears the account's pinned Google identity (users.google_sub), audited, but only when a working password remains so the account cannot lock itself out.

endpoints.guard: none (public; password_door_open(db), per-account brute-force limiter, refuse_disabled_sign_in)
endpoints.summary: Verifies email and scrypt password and either sets the session cookie (retiring other devices) or, when OTP is required, emails a six-digit login code and returns a challenge; 403 when the password door is shut.

endpoints.guard: none (public; per-account code limiter, consume_user_code, refuse_disabled_sign_in)
endpoints.summary: Spends the six-digit code the password step emailed and issues the session cookie, retiring every other device.
Bumps users.token_version so the token is revoked and deletes the session cookie; used by the shell's Sign out on every screen and by My account.

Returns the signed-in account's session claims plus live capabilities, a student's feature switches, Google-link state, the last ten sign-ins and notification preferences; the SPA's authGuard calls it on every signed-in route.
Merges a partial map of email preferences (today only sign_in_alerts) into users.notification_prefs, audited.

endpoints.guard: none (proof is the PURPOSE_ONBOARD_SET ticket from step 2; barred accounts refused; password_problem policy)
endpoints.summary: Step 3 of onboarding: spends the 15-minute ticket, sets the account's password hash, revokes the setup link and sends the student to the login screen without signing them in.

endpoints.guard: none (proof is the PURPOSE_ONBOARD setup-link token + matching email typed back; barred accounts refused)
endpoints.summary: Step 1 of onboarding: peeks (does not spend) the setup link, checks the typed address matches the account, and emails a six-digit code to it.

endpoints.guard: none (proof is the setup-link token + the emailed PURPOSE_ONBOARD_CODE, consumed atomically)
endpoints.summary: Step 2 of onboarding: spends the six-digit code and returns a 15-minute ticket that is the only thing the password step accepts.

endpoints.guard: reset token (auth_tokens, PURPOSE_RESET); refuses a barred account
endpoints.summary: Consumes a one-hour reset link to set a new password, revokes other pending reset links and signs the account out of every device without signing anybody in.
Retires every session the account holds, including this device, by bumping token_version, and writes an audit row.

endpoints.guard: none (public; refuses with /login?error=sso_config when Google is not configured)
endpoints.summary: Mints a state and nonce, stores them in a short-lived cookie and redirects the browser to Google's consent screen.

endpoints.guard: none (public; single-use state cookie + nonce, verified Google ID token, roster lookup, google_sub pin)
endpoints.summary: Google redirects here after consent; the server verifies the ID token, admits only an email already on the roster (pinning google_sub on first use), retires other sessions, records the sign-in, optionally mails a sign-in alert, sets the reep_session cookie and redirects to the role's home.
Tells the login screen whether Google sign-in is configured, whether the password door is open (derived from whether any account holds a real scrypt hash) and the institution's mail domain.

endpoints.guard: get_ws_session cookie + Origin check; role STUDENT or ADMIN (_is_rehearsal) else close 1008; student.assistant feature switch (close 4016); live consent (4013); concurrency and daily/attempt caps (1013/4012/4015)
endpoints.summary: WebSocket that relays 24 kHz PCM between the browser and Amazon Nova 2 Sonic for a phased mock interview, writing the session record, transcript turns, scorecard and (when all three switches allow) WAV recordings; the Main Admin's rehearsal runs the same interview with every writer off.
Returns the caller's live consent acknowledgement for the current terms version (or null) plus the provider label; loaded by the interview room on the page and in the dock.

endpoints.guard: get_current_session + role == STUDENT (403 otherwise); version must match INTERVIEW_CONSENT_VERSION

request_path: 1. Phone: an Angular component (e.g. a mentor screen) calls fetch(`${environment.apiBase}/mentor/students/{id}/ledger`, {credentials:'include'}); apiBase='/api' (apps/web/src/environments/environment.ts), so the request is same-origin and the httpOnly reep_session cookie is attached.

2. Service worker apps/web/public/reep-sw.js: its fetch listener matches same-origin /api/ and calls event.stopImmediatePropagation() before ngsw-worker.js's listener (imported second), calls no respondWith, so the browser does the network request itself. Nothing is cached (no ngsw dataGroups, rule 1).
3. DNS (external, not in code) resolves reep.sast-skills.com to the CloudFront distribution. TLS 1.3 (TLSv1.3_2025) terminates at the edge with the us-east-1 ACM certificate.

4. AWS WAF web ACL reep-edge (us-east-1, CLOUDFRONT scope) evaluates aws-common (CommonRuleSet, 5 body/size rules counted), aws-bad-inputs, rate-limit (2000/5 min/IP), then body-rules-outside-uploads (blocks body-rule labels unless the request is multipart/form-data). A block is a 403 at the edge with a non-JSON body.

5. CloudFront /api/* behaviour (infra/cdk/reep_core/stack.py additional_behaviors): redirect-to-HTTPS, ALLOW_ALL methods, CachingDisabled, AllViewer origin-request policy (forwards cookie, headers, query). The SPA-fallback function is not attached here. Origin api-alb = origin.reep.sast-skills.com over HTTPS TLS 1.2 with a 60 s read timeout. The request line goes to the reep-cloudfront-logs bucket without query, cookie or referer.

6. ALB reep-alb in the public subnets. Its SG admits 443 only from CloudFront prefix list pl-9aa247f3. The HTTPS :443 listener uses ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06 and the ap-south-1 ACM certificate, with idle timeout 300 s and drop_invalid_header_fields. The default action forwards to target group reep-api (HTTP :3300, IP targets, health /ready, 600 s deregistration delay). The access log goes to the reep-alb-logs bucket.
7. ECS Fargate task of service api (cluster reep, family reep-api, ARM64, private subnet). SG api admits 3300 only from the ALB SG. The task is one of 2-10 autoscaled replicas.

8. uvicorn, from the Dockerfile CMD: python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 3300 --proxy-headers, with FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=10.42.0.0/16 so X-Forwarded-For/Proto from the ALB are trusted. It builds the ASGI scope and calls the FastAPI app object in apps/api-py/app/main.py.

9. Middleware, outermost first. Starlette 1.3.1's add_middleware inserts at index 0, so the last one added runs outermost: ServerErrorMiddleware -> _security_headers (@app.middleware('http'): nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, HSTS) -> RequestTraceMiddleware (app/traceability.py: takes or mints X-Request-ID and writes a reep.access log line with rid= to CloudWatch /reep/api) -> CORSMiddleware (allow_origins=[settings.web_origin], credentials) -> ExceptionMiddleware. The Sentry FastAPI integration (init_sentry in app/observability.py at import) opens a transaction scrubbed by app/telemetry_scrub.py.
10. Routing: app.include_router(mentee_records.router, prefix='/api') matches GET /api/mentor/students/{student_id}/ledger -> read_student_ledger in apps/api-py/app/routers/mentee_records.py.

11. Session dependency get_current_session (app/identity.py) reads the reep_session cookie and calls security.verify_session_token (app/security.py). That does a PyJWT HS256 decode with settings.auth_secret (AUTH_SECRET from Secrets Manager reep/app), then account_state(userId): a cached SELECT of users.token_version, disabled_at, deleted_at. It refuses a token whose version is behind (one device at a time) or whose account is barred. Failure is 401 'Sign in required.' plus X-Reep-Session: retired when session_was_retired(). _with_live_mentor_id adds mentorId.

12. DB dependency get_db (app/db.py) opens a Session from SessionLocal. The engine is create_engine(settings.sqlalchemy_url, psycopg 3, pool_pre_ping, pool_size=10, max_overflow=10 from the task env DB_POOL_SIZE/DB_MAX_OVERFLOW).

13. Gates in the handler: require_capability(db, session, 'mentor.mentees') (app/governance.py: role baseline + derived mentor functions + live capability_grants rows, else 403), then rule 2's _assert_can_access_student(session, student_id, db, allow_handover=True) (routers/mentor.py, delegating to policies.assert_student_scope: a MENTOR sees only their own Mentor group, the ADMIN sees all, a read-only 90-day handover grant applies; refusal is 404). Simpler routes use the role gates require_mentor / require_admin in routers/mentor.py or require_staff in policies.py.

14. Domain read: load_day(db, student_id, target) in routers/student_programme.py (target from app/clock.local_today, Asia/Kolkata) issues SQLAlchemy 2.0 selects. psycopg 3 sends them over TCP 5432 inside the private subnets to RDS reep-postgres (PostgreSQL 17, db reep_py, SG db admits only the api SG, single-AZ db.t4g.small).
15. Return: compose_ledger builds the Pydantic v2 response_model LedgerOut and FastAPI serialises it to JSON. get_db's finally closes the Session and returns the connection to the pool.

16. Back out: CORS headers, X-Request-ID echo and access line with status/duration, security headers, Sentry transaction finished -> uvicorn -> ALB target group -> HTTPS listener -> CloudFront (CachingDisabled, so not stored) -> phone. reep-sw.js did not intercept, so the real status reaches the page, and the Angular component updates its signal.
